note: ABI vector cases come from abi_vectors.json (P04-ABI-nnn); local-event record vectors and debounce traces come from event_vectors.json (P04-EVT-nnn, P04-DEB-nnn); the silence-priming scenarios come from priming_vectors.json (P04-PRM-nnn) and each planted priming defect is a case (P04-PRMDEF-nn). Each invariant maps to named Rust tests, which run only under central verification, so P04-RUST-CENTRAL is blocked until that run exists.

cases.needs: cargo test -p franken-hal (the count printed by the runner), cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings and cargo fmt --all -- --check, each via RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1 rch exec. Every behavioral invariant below is a named Rust test; this runner never builds.

a separate true-device qualification ledger. Nothing here exercises a board: the fake device is a model, and the E04 matrix still has every interface field unknown, so open_hardware refuses a real device.

invariants.text: malformed device responses (geometry, event records, byte counts) fail muted
driver errors fail muted; a failed submit quarantines its slot; a vanished device is persistent
wire records are big-endian on any host, with hand-computed golden vectors
the fake device is labelled model evidence; a real device needs an eligible contract
forgetting or dropping a submit token cannot return storage
a cancelled or timed-out drain quarantines and never claims success
stale, duplicate and unknown completions never free the new occupant
storage the kernel may hold is never freed or reused, under any interleaving
quarantine and leaking are bounded; saturation is recorded
destroying the owner or its table does not free storage the kernel may still read
a copying-write ABI avoids leases only with stated evidence; a retained ABI keeps the slot
stop requested is distinct from an acknowledged stop; unknown stop deadline refuses audible transition
device counters wrap but never claim more than is in flight; a counter that goes backwards, even by one, faults muted and credits nothing
only an acknowledged reset frees quarantined storage; an unacknowledged mute blocks everything
submits are validated before anything changes; a full ring is a typed busy error
session ids come from a 32-bit counter (no 64-bit atomics on mips/ppc32) that never wraps and refuses new sessions once exhausted, so an old token can never match a new session
a clean prepare, run, drain, close cycle works and leaks nothing
the local-event record is big-endian and strictly decoded: bad sync, unknown kind, nonzero flags and short records are refused
an unsupported or unevidenced local-event capability is refused before any read; a declared one opens
a button edge is reported only after it has been steady for the window, on the channel's own tick; bounces restart the wait and are counted
partial reads are reassembled, a stalled one is discarded, garbage resynchronises, and the split of a valid stream never changes what is delivered
repeated bad records or reads fault the channel (reset recovers it); a vanished device leaves buttons unknown and is not recoverable
the event queue and the torn-record buffer are bounded; a fault is lost only when nothing else can make room, and that is counted and marks the evidence incomplete
logging never changes what the session does: the wrapper returns what the bare session returns under a healthy, refusing, full or unavailable sink
a fault is logged once with its cause; a lost fault record is counted and marks the evidence incomplete; a full sink drops ordinary events before a fault
every call is logged in order with the state it left, as one JSON line with the documented keys, pseudonymized and carrying no audio, labelled model evidence

HalSession emits an event at each transition that exists (prepare, start, an acknowledged stop or reset, every recorded fault, a device lost while faulted), in order, with the frames accepted at that moment; a lost completion yields the timeout and the quarantine saturation; an unacknowledged mute and a lost device are each emitted once

the event queue is the same bounded, critical-first queue the local-event channel uses: never over its cap, ordinary events dropped first, a fault lost only when nothing else can make room; a flood is bounded and every event is delivered, queued, dropped, evicted or lost, with a gap in seq showing the loss
emission never changes what the session does: an unread or tiny event queue gives the same results and receipt as a healthy one, and a queue that could hold nothing is a bad configuration

log records carry the events the session itself emitted, not a receipt diff: events waiting before wrapping are reported once, events already taken are not repeated, and a fault the session's own queue lost is reported, noted in the diagnostic log and marks the evidence incomplete

an optional silence-priming requirement (default none, so an existing session is unchanged) is enforced by HalSession::start before it touches the device: only a whole all-zero block the device took in full while the session was prepared counts, so a tone, one non-zero sample, a short block, a partial or refused take and anything submitted while unmuted do not; the count is discarded by a stop, a reset, a fault and a lost device and spent by the unmute; and each of those rules is refused by name when it is planted wrong
the runner's comparison is not vacuous
files, shared vectors, mapping and hygiene hold
what cannot be verified here is counted as blocked, never passed

not_covered: Local button, LED and fault events: the adapter logic exists and is tested against a fake byte source, but the 8-byte record is a harness model. No retained driver is known to emit it. E04 analysed the audio-control handler but mapped no command number to a local-event capability or record, so the capability for a real board stays Unsupported and no real event source exists.

Event emission: HalSession emits transitions into a bounded, critical-first queue and LoggedSession reports them, but the events are transitions, so there is nothing to debounce (the shared part is the queue policy). A repeated identical fault is not coalesced: a flood is bounded and counted, not merged. The wrapper allocates a receipt per call (a harness and diagnostics layer, not the render loop), the queue is heap-backed, and the timebase is a call count and an event sequence number, not wall time.

Silence priming: the gate is a host model. It is off by default, nothing here claims a board needs priming, and what a real device does with silence queued before start, and the board's safe startup order (EXT-E04-AMP-SEQUENCE), are unknown. A consumer that wants priming states the block count itself.
Real-driver adapters: none, by design. The E04 matrix is still entirely unknown, so there is no admitted driver ABI to adapt.
Migration of franken-speaker onto HalSession: it still uses the offline typestate, whose finish_drain_and_close frees quarantined slots without any acknowledgment.
